title: Atomic focus & gesture handling for density transitions in virtual table
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:

We need a cohesive design for how focus states, keyboard gestures, and pointer interactions behave when the table switches density (comfortable -> compact -> dense) and while columns are being resized or re-ordered in a virtualized render window. Current issues: focus jumps when virtualization re-measures rows during density animation, keyboard developers see surprising tab order changes, and drag handles feel jittery when the underlying DOM is recycled.

Background:

Recent engineering work to increase virtualization efficiency introduced a measure-pass that reuses row DOM nodes and changes transforms during density transitions. This improved performance but exposed UX regressions: 1) cell focus can be lost or rebound to a different column after a density change, 2) column drag handles detach visually while the pointer is still down, and 3) aria attributes are sometimes out of sync during quick sort/filter operations.

Goals:

- Define atomic focus rules so keyboard users keep context when density or virtualization reflow occurs.
- Specify pointer/gesture tolerances and visual affordances for column resize/drag across density animations.
- Provide accessible sorting/filter semantics that remain consistent while rows/columns are recycled.
- Give engineering clear, implementable constraints (timing, CSS strategies, aria expectations) and acceptance criteria for QA.

Proposed approach (high level):

1) Focus sticky token: introduce a transient focus token model. When a cell receives focus, components store a {rowKey, colKey, focusPhase} token in a stable layer (not DOM-derived). On re-render, runtime reconciles to nearest visible cell and restores focus programmatically if the original DOM was recycled.

2) Visual continuity for gestures: use CSS transforms for virtualization translation (GPU accelerated) and separate pointer-affordance layer for drag handles. Drag handles are rendered in a sibling overlay container that is not recycled with rows; it mirrors column positions.

3) Density transition choreography: define motion primitives for density changes (duration 160ms, cubic-bezier(0.2,0.9,0.2,1)) and an opt-in 'no-motion' accessibility flag tied to prefers-reduced-motion. During the transition, lock keyboard navigation to the focused row until animation end to avoid focus jump.

4) Sorting/filtering stability: on sort/filter actions, emit a stable announcer message via live region combined with aria-rowindex and aria-colindex updates. Ensure aria-sort attributes are updated atomically before any DOM recycling to avoid screen reader noise.

Tradeoffs and notes:

- Storing a focus token outside of DOM increases reconciliation complexity but preserves keyboard context; this requires a small runtime API change.
- Drag handle overlay simplifies gestures but needs a stable column measurement feed; there will be additional bookkeeping when columns resize concurrently.
- Adding animation locks can slightly delay focus updates by the transition duration; keep short durations to minimize latency.

Links to artifacts:

- Figma flows + component frames: https://www.figma.com/file/ExampleTableFlows/Redwood-Table-Patterns (section: Density & Focus)
- Design spec (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/UX/pages/Table+Density+Focus+Spec
- Engineering spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1824

Acceptance criteria (QAable):

- When toggling density while a cell is focused, focus remains on the same logical cell (by rowKey/colKey) after the transition completes.

- Column drag handles remain attached to pointer for the duration of drag even when virtualization recycles rows/columns.

- Screen reader announces sort changes exactly once and reads the new position/heading without interleaved noise.

- Keyboard navigation (arrow keys, tab) does not skip columns when a re-measure occurs during a density change.

- Prefers-reduced-motion disables density animation and focus locking behavior falls back to immediate reconcile.
